rules.title: Philadelphia ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Philadelphia Code § 9-813 restricts landlords' use of algorithmic rent-coordination or revenue-management services. Tenants in pending class actions allege that subscribing to and using RealPage services violates it. An aggrieved person may elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, plus equitable relief, interest, and attorney fees and costs. The precise prohibited conduct and definitions are not captured in the available source.
rules.key_value: $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages (aggrieved person's election), plus equitable relief, interest, attorney fees and costs

coverage.summary: Covered landlords, buildings and prohibited services are not stated in the available source; no building-size or construction-date limits are reported.

rules.effective_date_note: The only source, a secondary law-firm alert dated August 21, 2026, gives the effective date as 'February 2025' (month only). The exact day is not stated, so effective_date is left null. The law is in force as of the query date under any day in February 2025.
rules.quoted_span: Philadelphia’s ordinance permits an aggrieved person to elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, together with equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs.
rules.review_note: Supported only by a secondary source (Morgan Lewis LawFlash). The ordinance text, bill number, enactment date, exact effective date, definitions of covered services and exemptions are not captured; verify against the official Philadelphia Code. The source notes generally that local algorithmic-pricing ordinances may be challenged on municipal authority, punitiveness and retroactivity grounds. No Philadelphia-specific challenge is reported.
rules.source_notes: Secondary source reports that § 9-813 is at issue in Liu v. Willow Bridge Property Company LLC and RealPage Inc. (Phila. C.P.) and Jahanbakhsh v. Greystar. The candidate's requirement wording ('RealPage-type services') was narrowed to what the source states.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Private remedies include treble actual damages or $2,000 per violation
